assets.description:
The player's desk at the start of the game: the open-air workspace of a village sarpanch candidate in a fictional village in rural Bihar, north India. Seen from directly above: a flat top-down view with no perspective distortion.
Composition (16:9): a woven rope charpai with a wooden frame fills the middle two-thirds of the frame and serves as the desk. The centre of the charpai is left clear and uncluttered, because the game places a sheet of paper there. Along the top edge, the base of a thick neem tree trunk with gnarled roots; a tear-off wall calendar with blank pages hangs on a nail in the trunk. The ground around the charpai is packed earth with a few fallen neem leaves.
Objects, each clearly separated with space around it so it can be cut out later:
- left side: an old cream rotary landline phone with a coiled cord; a dented tin cash box
- on the charpai, near its edges: a red cloth-bound bahi-khata ledger; a folded newspaper whose columns are suggested by grey blocks with no readable letters; a small stack of paper files tied with cotton string; a small spiral notebook with a pencil
- right side: a glass of milky chai on a small steel saucer
- bottom-right corner: the front wheel and handlebars of an old black bicycle entering the frame
Dappled neem-leaf shadows fall across the scene.
assets.notes: Phase 0 style direction A. Exploration only: never exported.

assets.description:
The player's desk at the start of the game: the open-air workspace of a village sarpanch candidate in a fictional village in rural Bihar, north India, present day.
Composition (16:9): a woven rope charpai with a wooden frame fills the middle two-thirds of the frame and serves as the desk; its surface is seen from above. The centre of the charpai is left clear and uncluttered, because the game places a sheet of paper there. Along the top edge, the base of a thick neem tree trunk with roots; a tear-off wall calendar with blank pages hangs front-facing on a nail in the trunk. Neem foliage overhangs the two top corners. The ground is packed earth with a few fallen single leaflets.
Objects, each clearly separated with space around it so it can be cut out later:
- left side: a small wooden stool holding a cheap Android smartphone in a worn rubber case with a cracked screen guard, its screen dark and blank; below the stool, a dented deep-indigo painted tin cash box
- on the charpai, near its edges: a red cloth-bound bahi-khata ledger tied with string (top-left area); a folded newspaper whose columns are suggested by grey blocks with no readable letters (bottom-left area); a stack of paper files tied with cotton string (top-right area); a spiral writing pad with a pencil on it (bottom-right area); a small khaki cloth-bound pocket diary held shut with a rubber band, beside the writing pad but clearly separate from it
- right side, on the ground: a glass of milky chai on a small steel saucer
- bottom-right corner: the front wheel and handlebars of an old black bicycle with a bell, entering the frame

assets.description: The player's personal assistant: a young man of about 25 from the village, quick, loyal and a little anxious. Lean build, neatly combed hair, thin moustache, a checked half-sleeve shirt with a ballpoint pen clipped in the pocket, a cheap wristwatch.

The rival candidate: heir of the family that has held the village headship for decades; a man in his early fifties, confident, polished and charming, with a hint of menace. Heavy-set, thick greying moustache, gold-rimmed spectacles, a crisp off-white kurta with a maroon woollen shawl over one shoulder, a gold ring. Not a caricature.

A local construction contractor and brick-kiln owner of about 45 who funds candidates in return for future favours. Heavy, well-fed build, broad face, clean-shaven, neatly oiled hair, a plain solid maroon polo shirt with no checks or pattern, a thick gold chain and a chunky gold watch, a smartphone held near his chest. A friendly smile that does not quite reach his eyes. He must look clearly different from the young man in the reference image.

A young local reporter of about 27 who runs her own news channel from her phone; sharp, fearless, curious. Hair tied back, small earrings, a cotton kurta with a dupatta, a lanyard with a blank press card, holding a smartphone fitted with a small clip-on microphone.
A recurring villager: an elderly farmer of about 70, wiry and sun-weathered, white stubble, a checked cotton gamchha tied as a turban, an open shirt over a plain vest. Proud, tired, dignified.

A recurring villager: a woman of about 40 who leads the village women's self-help group; practical, outspoken and respected. Cotton saree with the pallu over her head, glass bangles, a cloth bag on her shoulder.

A recurring villager: an unemployed graduate of about 24, restless and frustrated. Clean-shaven with NO moustache, thin black rectangular spectacles, slightly long side-parted hair, a plain pale-pink full-sleeve formal shirt with no checks or pattern, a plastic folder of job applications held against his chest (no visible text). He must look clearly different from the young man in the reference image.

Camera override: seen from directly above, flat top-down. A hand-painted illustrated map of the fictional village, like a painted board: several distinct neighbourhoods (tolas) of mud-and-brick houses with tiled and tin roofs separated by dirt lanes; a central chowk with a tea stall and a big peepal tree on a raised platform; a primary school with a small playground; a public well and a handpump; a small pond; a small simple temple and a small simple mosque in different neighbourhoods; a dirt road entering from the left edge; green and mustard-yellow fields with irrigation channels around the outskirts; a few neem and mango trees. Every area is visually distinct and separated so each can be clicked. No labels, no text, no people.

Camera override: eye level, from where the candidate sits. The village chaupal where villagers bring their grievances: a raised platform of old brick under a large banyan tree with hanging aerial roots and broad, simple, oval glossy leaves. A worn striped durrie rug in the foreground. The middle third of the frame is an open, empty space where a villager will stand (added later as a separate portrait), so keep it free of people and objects. Background: a lane with a few mud-brick houses, a handpump, a buffalo resting in the distance.

Camera override: eye level, from just behind the speaker at the lectern. Foreground: the back edge of a simple wooden lectern with a blank notepad on it, marigold garlands strung along the front edge of the stage, two horn loudspeakers on bamboo poles at the sides, a blank cloth banner (no writing) strung across the top of the frame. Beyond the stage: an open dusty field and, at the horizon, trees and village houses. The field is EMPTY of people, because the crowd is added later as separate sprites.

Camera override: eye level. A vote-counting hall in a block office on counting day: long tables in rows with blank tally sheets, grey steel ballot boxes with paper seals, bundles of blank ballot papers tied with string, a wire-mesh barricade in front of rows of empty plastic chairs for counting agents, a ceiling fan and tube lights, a large blank whiteboard on the back wall for results. No people (they are added later).

Four different ordinary villagers from the same village, each chest-up in a three-quarter view with a calm, natural expression, as portraits for people who come to the candidate with their problems. In order: a woman of about 35 in a printed cotton saree; an old man of about 75 with a white beard and a woollen cap; a teenage girl of about 16 in a school uniform with two braids; a man of about 40 in a sweat-stained vest with a gamchha on his shoulder. Each is an individual with real dignity; no caricature.
